Background picture for a 2D side-view narrative game, made as a Japanese multi-block colour woodblock print of the late Edo period landscape genre (ukiyo-e, nishiki-e), showing a foreign northern harbour the way a Japanese printmaker of the 1850s would have drawn it.

Technique: a black key block prints crisp, fine outlines of even width (about 3 pixels) around every shape, ending in slightly tapered points where the carver's knife stopped. Inside the outlines every colour is a flat, even area printed from its own block: no modelling, no shading, no cast shadows, no highlights, no texture brushwork. The only gradients are bokashi, the soft wiped-ink gradations of woodblock printing, always running from one edge of an area: the sky starts with a dark Prussian-blue band along the very top edge, fades to a pale blue-grey and then to a warm orange and pink glow just above the horizon; the sea is deep Prussian blue at the horizon and fades lighter towards the quay. A small set of printing inks: Prussian blue, indigo, vermilion red, soft beni pink, yellow ochre, pale mineral green, grey sumi ink and the warm off-white of the paper. Decorative flat patterns the way prints show them: the cottage and the quay as outlined flat stones, the slate roof as rows of fine parallel lines, the rocks of the headland as outlined flat masses with small dots of blue-green moss, the wooden planks with a few fine grain lines, low clouds as long horizontal mist bands with rounded ends in pink and pale blue. Flat Japanese pictorial space: layered planes, a high clear horizon, everything sharp, no atmospheric haze, no glow, no bloom, no lens effects. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not an oil or watercolour painting, not a modern anime illustration, not a postcard, not a vector illustration with gradients.

Things that are animated separately and must not be painted: the water is calm flat bokashi colour without any wave lines, ripples, foam, spray or reflections; the lighthouse lamp only as a small flat yellow spot without any beam, rays or glow; the lantern glass flat pale yellow without glow; no smoke from the chimney; no birds.

Composition: the horizon at about 40 % of the picture height. The harbour-master's cottage stands at the far left edge, its front wall with the lit window and the door facing the viewer, the chimney against the sky. The lighthouse stands on its rocky headland at the right edge, the tower rising high into the sky, the rocks reaching down into the sea. The calm sea fills the middle band between the horizon and the quay; the short wooden jetty with the two moored fishing boats lies in the middle distance, left of the centre. The stone quay is a broad, level, empty walking surface running across the whole width of the picture from about 64 % to 84 % of the picture height, seen slightly from above, with its stone front edge at the bottom. The barrels, the stack of crates and the rope coil stand at the right end of the quay; the lantern post stands on the quay between the centre and the right. Keep the middle and the left half of the quay empty. No frame, no border, no title cartouche, no seal stamps, no calligraphy.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.
